name: Jaime Harrison
subject: Annie is going to win this.
disclaimer_text: Paid for by VPP
body:
| [](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/116551?t=6&akid=26081%2E878179%2EJbMH9m) Folks, I know what it takes to run against Lindsey Graham.

I know what it feels like to stand on a stage in South Carolina and make the case that this state deserves better — that our families deserve better. I know what it costs to build something from the ground up against a machine with decades of money and power behind it.

And I know, as well as anyone, that it matters deeply who steps up to take on that fight.

**That's why I'm proud to officially endorse Dr. Annie Andrews for United States Senate.**[If you’re able, please split a donation between Voter Protection Project and her campaign right now. »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/116551?t=7&akid=26081%2E878179%2EJbMH9m) | [DONATE NOW »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/116551?t=8&akid=26081%2E878179%2EJbMH9m)
---
Lindsey Graham has had 22 years in that Senate seat, and our state keeps ranking near the bottom. That's not a coincidence. That's a choice he made — again and again — to put his political survival ahead of the people of South Carolina.

Annie Andrews is different. I've gotten to know her, and I’m proud to call her my friend. She is a pediatrician who has spent her career taking care of children others might have overlooked. She is a mom who understands the weight of the daily decisions families have to make. _And she is a candidate who is doing this because she believes — genuinely — that South Carolina families deserve a Senator who fights for them._

That combination is rare. And it is exactly what this moment requires.

I ran against Lindsey Graham in 2020. We earned more votes than any Democrat ever in SC. We started a movement that has only gotten stronger over the past six years. I saw firsthand what is possible when a grassroots movement believes in something and refuses to quit. **The landscape has only shifted further in our favor since then. The energy is real. The urgency is real.**

But this does not happen without resources.

[If you've been waiting for a moment to get behind this race, this is it. Will you split a donation between Dr. Annie Andrews and Voter Protection Project today to help make South Carolina's Senate seat everything it should have been all along? »](https://act.protectvoting.org/go/116551?t=9&akid=26081%2E878179%2EJbMH9m)

---|---|---
Graham Platner in yet another video he's made to deny allegations levied against him during this campaign on July 6, 2026.
[For months, we've been telling Angry Democrat readers who Graham Platner actually is.](https://substack.com/redirect/d040469e-491e-4bc9-b830-ea81b9987845?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) Not the working-class oyster farmer on the yard signs. A candidate two Democratic Socialist organizers found at his home in Sullivan, packaged by the strategist who built Zohran Mamdani's campaign, and sold to a national donor base as an everyman ([Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/393cc0c6-0ab6-415b-96e3-893947220328?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). I did not report that to help Susan Collins. I reported it because voters deserve to know who is asking for their trust before November, not after.
On July 6, another woman accused Platner of sexual assault, and the campaign has told supporters he needed time to "reflect on the best path forward" ([CNN](https://substack.com/redirect/9b259c67-3739-44c8-a06f-24ea1e8835b9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg); [NBC News](https://substack.com/redirect/66607fde-4884-4b6d-ae60-7807fe30fd0b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). He denies the allegation. He calls it "troubling, serious, and false," and that denial belongs next to every sentence that follows. Nobody who has watched this campaign should be surprised. The party built this candidate, and the party endorsed him already knowing what the issues were.
## Its Always Another Story
In June, The New York Times published three women from past relationships who described his behavior as unsettling, demeaning, and in one case physically threatening ([Washington Post timeline](https://substack.com/redirect/5e08d772-3aa2-484f-bef9-da1aa3645c06?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). The Wall Street Journal reported he traded sexually explicit messages with multiple women near the start of his marriage, and his own campaign confirmed it. In 2013, on Reddit, he told people worried about sexual assault to "take some responsibility for themselves and not get so fucked up they wind up having sex with someone they don't mean to" ([The Maine Monitor](https://substack.com/redirect/9362af69-007a-41a9-8e0d-36edad478379?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). Those are his words, not an accuser's.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/4ab4e364-3142-462f-9bb0-830fb4002187?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Hans Landa wearing a cap with the Totenfopf in Inglorious Basterds in 2009. Of the 8 Oscars this movie was nominated for, it won only one: Best Supporting Actor for Christoph Waltz, who played this character.
Platner also has a Totenkopf tattoo, the death's head the SS wore guarding Hitler's camps, inked on his chest. He says he never knew what it meant. The record cuts against him. In Reddit threads from 2019 and 2020 he discussed the Totenkopf and SS lightning bolts by name, and his own political director said a man who prides himself on military history could not plausibly have stayed ignorant for eighteen years ([CNN KFile](https://substack.com/redirect/b4fa5740-bf0a-4f41-8fb9-d6fb1a87731a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). Now, Jenny Racicot says he forced her to have sex with him in 2021, an account a later boyfriend says she shared at the time and that her emails with her therapist corroborate ([NPR](https://substack.com/redirect/5590332a-7bd0-4c31-bac5-284c0f8a09fa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)). He denies that too.
I am not the jury on the 2021 allegation. I will not call a denied accusation a conviction, and I will not wave off a corroborated one because the target is inconvenient. The argument does not need a verdict. It's hard to believe that three women in the Times, and his own campaign's confirmations, and his own posts, all add up to nothing.
_If you want this kind of reporting, the kind the Democratic party will not do about itself, subscribe. The Angry Democrat runs on facts, not loyalty_

### They Knew
The party's problem is not that this surfaced. The party's problem is when...

[Go here for more actions](https://default.salsalabs.org/Tf09d3032-62b6-4a82-b82d-00627e789f74/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9))_ **[If Washington Won’t Defend the Constitution, the States Must Join Together to Do it](https://default.salsalabs.org/T985b798c-4f06-4e06-8e15-d2a062cbff33/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Trump is shredding the Constitution, Congressional Republicans are cheering him on, and the Supreme Court isn’t doing a damn thing to stop him. **[If Washington Won’t Defend the Constitution, the States Must Join Together to Do it](https://default.salsalabs.org/T8d45f6fc-008a-467d-9e07-96b6165f2808/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)** Too many Americans are still acting as if this is just politics as usual. It’s not. And with federal guardrails all but gone, states must step in. Governors, state attorneys general, and other key officials who still believe in the Constitution should form a Constitutional defense pact: a coordinated, lawful effort to protect elections, civil liberties, public servants, and the rule of law from presidential abuse of power. That means coordinating lawsuits. Working together against attacks that cross state lines. And if another state requests help protecting elections, public safety, or constitutional rights from actual attacks, other states should provide lawful mutual aid: legal teams, cybersecurity support, emergency personnel, election protection resources, and, where necessary to prevent violence, National Guard or state emergency support. This is not about partisanship. It is about defending the Constitution. And if red states want to join in, great. But if they can’t even take the simple step of pledging to defend the Constitution, that itself will speak volumes. **[Sign: If Washington Won’t Defend the Constitution, the States Must Join Together to Do it](https://default.salsalabs.org/T26f314b6-dfa7-4569-a18d-4dec15dee9cd/368d17ff-e836-4168-8049-c5f0900fbbf9)**

The House passed Republicans' reconciliation package in a razor-thin 215-214 vote last year, and while many think it was politics as usual... **they have absolutely gutted the American Dream.** It's a bill that includes the most drastic overhaul to Medicaid since the program was founded. They called it the "Big Beautiful Bill."
At the forefront of the vote was none other than my opponent Scott Desjarlais. His career before bowing to MAGA's agenda was being a physician. **How do you go from serving families to voting to cut roughly $700 billion from Medicaid? You** _**don 't**_**without betraying millions of Americans.**_**This came straight from his website:**_
| [](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/305ad935-a721-44ad-9147-188273c34294?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|

[HELP US HERE!](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/86f79a3a-c5e2-4b77-b43e-07ac9065e78d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
My fight is for protecting Medicaid and never voting to pull the rug out from under the people who need it most; not for a tax cut, not for a headline, not for anyone.
The primary is in a month. We need the resources to reach every voter in this district before then. Our families deserve a fighter in Congress, not another yes vote on bills passed in the dead of night.

name: Lt. Gen. (Ret.) William G. Boykin
subject: It was radical then, and it’s radical now
body:
250 years ago, our forefathers declared that we are endowed by our Creator with certain unalienable rights.

| | | | | |
---
|
---
[ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=1dd3e04988924f3c964a7184f7239327&_e=yhdIvdNz7_QaotmtHU0hnWY6GbDFfaVhkdKkreWlHg3vlZUZCCmoxmscnJFyISkRpomL3xS8WOhNHR7Lu16mWQoYKDl4rfEX3iHbj7JP1mhAXFfyhHoZj9ge9zw6AdINPHRQTk5YSImp7X7OAfnqaJ9VyKdex4KiF6QSfU5WAdzlIXMlVNVBP5l1gEWUK6WnwTyZ-FLa4zFl4x_ve2NcWcA1M2kTHJdqGZikoyVInAizb7_oMcqL_ZQ6MdmiI8P-Ut2rXqCCpaVaKDeDtkTuVTlfurSOFtvl6FvH9Qx09kogTzu-C6y3DdG9kdEHNgUj211NLtWDjltvNi-s0w_Ai5Uetg8rWK608kED20nuqCQ_dv6toz-__AemDy53pq8treehaHiqqk52Bj0ynHjNNJOKJJ6NGH4h7zd2-OZBsnFJU69qDmkH-6Icj_h2T4vyAWXa30F1ERq1DsKvtN5GrfNbflEdE6xjkFr77S8H86B3wm3_vh93z8y2p8_Yu7OKidfBzlShw0nV70l1hCZAyw%3D%3D)
---
Dear Faithful Friend,
250 years ago, our forefathers declared that we are endowed by our Creator with certain unalienable rights.
They were making it clear not only to King George III but to the world that _**America was not going to be just another country. ** _
**She was born instead of a moral purpose – a recognition that liberty is a gift solely from the God who gave us life, and that this nation would stand or fall depending on whether we remained anchored to Him. **
That idea was radical in 1776, it remains radical today, and defending that God-given liberty on the battlefield is something I’ve dedicated my life to.
**Over the course of my nearly 40 years in uniform, I served in Vietnam, was an original member and eventual commander of Delta Force, commanded our special operators in Mogadishu during Black Hawk Down, hunted Pablo Escobar in the jungles of Colombia, and led the capture of dictator Manuel Noriega in Panama.**
It’s been the honor of my life to serve amongst heroes willing to bleed and die to protect the liberties given to us by God. **And yet, I can’t take my mind off the more than 388 million poor souls across this planet who are being hunted, imprisoned, and killed just for practicing the same faith that shaped this country from its beginning.**
**In Nigeria, more than** _**100,000 Christians have been massacred ** _since 2009, their churches burned, their families driven into displacement. In Sudan, _churches are being bombed and survivors are being crucified_. In North Korea, _owning a Bible means a lifetime in a labor camp_. In China, _pastors are disappearing into re-education camps._ And across nearly a dozen Muslim-majority nations, the law itself mandates _death for anyone who leaves Islam and embraces Christ._
---
[ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=1dd3e04988924f3c964a7184f7239327&_e=yhdIvdNz7_QaotmtHU0hnWY6GbDFfaVhkdKkreWlHg3vlZUZCCmoxmscnJFyISkRpomL3xS8WOhNHR7Lu16mWQoYKDl4rfEX3iHbj7JP1mhAXFfyhHoZj9ge9zw6AdINPHRQTk5YSImp7X7OAfnqaJ9VyKdex4KiF6QSfU5WAdysKbsAHLsD0aHaJxwm_qqq2HTFYKaCoJKA4p5uDzYsl2-TjKguxHxwsaqr9EJrnM_oq3VCpf1HZaEqliMDn2AE9Eom3xBortADxFHH7RjWryl8j5Pcifqq-lho4HN75a1ZFLWAquCmeAyz0SLx1nXdtMpGGRlD3x33HavYwEYA3_nTOoE74L9E1itN95ZcURX_ceMVdhVlPES-QKOe6eT5Y6PObgbQn9y6CJYul5CNwrUZcErdLxMt_MVbQHwjofeXT5yawcVHnNUdag4iUamcLC2pKtxlp0AVQ1B9IUq_WQ7J5Oh7htQ2UiTXDo7ExhhgKScBo1C1yjL_ZaKMESEdyrkj7dW4NS8D2CrPMCrr3g%3D%3D)
---
**So as we mark this 250th anniversary, I am calling upon you to help make it a moment of rededication.** Not just to the ideals of the founding, but to the God who made those ideals possible.
If America is to carry her purpose into the next 250 years, I believe it will be because the Body of Christ rose up, remembered who it was, and refused to be silent.
**There is no organization in this nation more committed to that fight than Save the Persecuted Christians** – where I am honored to serve as a board member. Whether it’s the _growing awareness of the active genocide against Nigeria’s Christians_ (and recent U.S. action to help stop it), or the recent and very real _victories against the rise of sharia and Islamism here in America_ , it is due in large part to the relentless advocacy and education campaigns of Save the Persecuted Christians and the coalition of 200+ organizations they help to guide.
**Now I am asking you to be part of what comes next...**
This summer – _the summer of America's 250th birthday_ – **Save the Persecuted Christians is launching a national campaign to carry the message of persecuted Christians into churches, communities, and the halls of government across this country. **
**The goal is to raise $250,000 to fund that effort: educational events, coalition action, and a sustained push to ensure that this summer's celebration of ** _**American** _ **liberty is accompanied by a serious reckoning with what is happening to Christians who have none.**
[ _**That is the mission, and I am humbly but urgently asking you to help us meet it.** _ ](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=1dd3e04988924f3c964a7184f7239327&_e=yhdIvdNz7_QaotmtHU0hnWY6GbDFfaVhkdKkreWlHg3vlZUZCCmoxmscnJFyISkRpomL3xS8WOhNHR7Lu16mWQoYKDl4rfEX3iHbj7JP1mhAXFfyhHoZj9ge9zw6AdINPHRQTk5YSImp7X7OAfnqaJ9VyKdex4KiF6QSfU5WAdzo7WrrbMoqSaoccu895SaYE8GxW4xExBUb870Rzaafi1NefjwzUcV02c5-07vHphDmjAo97EC10412bQZS8eQp0KkQ_mR2ackS45AMQFLbWazoy2_UEqox2ZqNkgOgsA3XcZOl7oStO32yd19uG-EW09ID9w93mNehh3BEO9E5QsBW9X_VPUIkg1PjeX8EaB_uoQ3c2kHCUEtCRyMVD0vGh-AXuWdAxpag51xJl50HdqkIdxrq8IluxguskxvhPo0ePkO-zsLUdowIAiLij2_xIHN5uXtk739xqt6lYVmznSTtju8lRw8bTlygv-A5Yf_3USRPNsG6sCxVK8ljnnw58rh5ar4ss8QhZ-cBJHZpGg%3D%3D)
---
| [PLEASE GIVE TODAY](https://links.stayinformednow.net/u/click?_t=c02d37b0057e4505a2324dee8ee3dc76&_m=1dd3e04988924f3c964a7184f7239327&_e=yhdIvdNz7_QaotmtHU0hnWY6GbDFfaVhkdKkreWlHg3vlZUZCCmoxmscnJFyISkRpomL3xS8WOhNHR7Lu16mWQoYKDl4rfEX3iHbj7JP1mhAXFfyhHoZj9ge9zw6AdINPHRQTk5YSImp7X7OAfnqaJ9VyKdex4KiF6QSfU5WAdwG1ucGgsNkrFRJgKrWzcanT9jirdWLXWomePlvViunCisFi-n-4VRb6W4Lu6YexQ7lAD0Xzvf0szicSsGPEuPO_rwywqlv2y_Yc_naZthzAD3Rf9NuNPyN8hpSy6zGvMQPUmPCfnDIx7FvyzD14_v8Y1iySb5cN4QA9cyMJH3us0PYP0V3T2599JyVXyFHa7RSa6I6Cj1xLQcft34omom56I8mA7ErFPDTYcONUQKRBZD6ODO22LT2Czgvd1Bd6nx4nzaX01O8Ny7rYrDnxVZ1POVPdVpDv9XUbWfLZljSPXvlKexUqlBV0VLjt0AA7uWrrXsAbqwx36JcERE4f00ipAD1NDs_8qFN_cy4YCSbsg%3D%3D "PLEASE GIVE TODAY")
---
The men who signed that Declaration in 1776 knew they were risking everything. They did it because they believed the cause was worth it – because they believed that what God had entrusted to them was not theirs to squander.
We are the heirs of that inheritance. And I believe our persecuted brothers and sisters around the world are counting on us to honor it.
**As we celebrate 250 years of God-given liberty, I pray that you will consider making a generous, tax-deductible gift to Save the Persecuted Christians. **
Your gift is not just charity. _It is ammunition in the spiritual war._ It is a declaration that we will not surrender the moral purpose for which this nation was raised up, and we will not abandon those who are paying the highest price for the faith we still get to practice openly.
Please – do not set this aside. **Make your gift today.**
In His service,
Lt. Gen. (Ret.) William G. Boykin Member, Board of Directors Save the Persecuted Christians

| | **Iran's Supreme Leader Held a "We Must Rise" Rally While America Celebrated. Iran's Official July 4 Ceremony Had a Clenched Fist on a Red and Black Flag. The Nuclear Window Is Now Day 16 of 60.**
---
| | While the United States celebrated its 250th birthday, Iran held official ceremonies under the slogan "We Must Rise" — accompanied by an image of Supreme Leader Khamenei's clenched fist on a red and black background. Per GoLocal Prov's overnight brief, this was Iran's official visual language for the same 24-hour period that America was launching 850,000 fireworks over the Lincoln Memorial. The symbolism was deliberate on both sides. Two countries actively exchanging strikes, negotiating a nuclear deal, and simultaneously staging the maximum possible contrast in public imagery. Both performances were for domestic audiences. Both were real.
---
| | Trump claimed in his July 4 speech that the US had "wiped out" Iran's military. This is not accurate and was not confirmed by the Pentagon. Iranian forces struck US bases in Kuwait and Bahrain on June 28 — a week after the speech's claim would begin to apply. IRGC commanders appeared publicly in Tehran on July 4. The Iranian Navy's capabilities in the Gulf remain operational. The nuclear infrastructure was damaged in the June 2025 strikes but not destroyed — which is why 21,800 pounds of enriched uranium still require a negotiated resolution. A president can say his country wiped out an enemy's military. He cannot make it true by saying it at a fireworks show.
---
Today is Day 16 of the 60-day nuclear window. Technical working groups are meeting in Doha this week. Iran's inflation remains at 88.6% and the $300 billion private investment fund is the primary economic lifeline the Iranian government can point to. Tehran needs the deal to work as much as Washington does. That mutual dependence is the only reason the negotiations continue through active strikes, through contradictory public statements, and through competing July 4 imagery. The deal may still hold. The 44 days remaining will answer the question.

I built my legal career here. I raised my two kids here with my wife Sandra of 32 years. Montana has always been home, and that is never going to change.

President Trump nominated me twice to be Montana's US Attorney. During my time in that role, we went after drug traffickers and violent criminals who were endangering our communities. We stood up to the cartels. We drove criminal prosecutions to a 20-year high. Montana families deserve to feel safe – and we delivered.

Fellow Patriot, I have never run for office before. But I am running now because the stakes have never been higher. Chuck Schumer has made Montana a top target. He knows that flipping this seat hands him back the Senate so he can stonewall President Trump's agenda.

| | Dear Fellow American,

Winston Churchill once described Russia as "a riddle, wrapped in a mystery, inside an enigma"--words that still ring true.

But given Russia's ongoing war with Ukraine--and Russia's role in the shifting balance of power in today's world--a better understanding of Russia is critical.

Since Peter the Great, Russia's place among nations has only grown. As it transformed itself from a regional backwater to a great power, its politics and culture influenced significant events in our own history from the American Revolution to today.

And during the Cold War period between World War Two and the fall of the Soviet Union in 1991, American-Russian relations became the focus of world attention.

**The need for a better understanding of post-Cold War Russia, in light of its current importance and its long history as one of the world 's great powers, is why Hillsdale College has created a [FREE online video series on Russia](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/pnThCkNyCC1VQgCtjr8pM8ikNH_L5LdMs9UK28rfDk2A7x4o_QQvVQnEqV0d3UtGKlKuzNi4QfEq0Wv-qOc8IcHC11VSQhVSAR2C0V9BPeAQpGf_yspvigshUp13ukvBZCF8V__CCVdXFwvec_7i__aIx4FrnG8XgQMXVxkzSxUDB9EJi1lt3rOXkBcQWt2Hihgo6825uv-gzRBBWWIaeg_RHIGe4PZFJmrAIgdrgWKS4YbBx24t6xw8j8Cv2gzRy5i5518eLJ47TgEllzM3nHXtDfQw8v39yGtXT8errKR8xe9hY_Qry6g2zmIscMe2QId_W2krrJ-NlgErCayn0L47TRe4K8OyXMZPwSJolT7uf9-mKnHDWG-tu_PadEwYWe6LXKCKkabUl3w8kMGVpNRMQ8cd/Niibok4qj_kzmGY7iewDhl_mO9-CgkeG/22). **

In our online video series, based on a conference held at Hillsdale College, you'll learn more about Russian history--with special attention to the period from the Russian Revolution through the fall of the Soviet Union.

The video series also explores Russia's significant contributions to literature, through such authors as Dostoyevsky and Tolstoy, and to classical music, through such composers as Tchaikovsky and Rachmaninoff.

**You 'll also gain a deeper understanding of Russia's relationship with the West today, and about the causes and complications of the current Ukraine war. **

You can receive instant access to this free video series right now using this secure link:

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/russia-cca](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/0OxmYB44SAM8OkWhRBFBTRz4TcuJvakkZQENoWPbZ5UClmE0uv7zjKr6kZ_KuN24UxR-LsT2uMtXsZF9hdWaEWJF_zQ2Wstm4SQpXAeGmXWw9B7HiyCt_wsM489YpqRTTLI7imC-xQO6zfw4_RXkCH477wJZgZOZo35Q0w5L4S9FNHysVC7vr8NHRoa-TY_SYosH4cDoj0UNhVy9iLdC4Fy3OJlns5OgEhHBngirAkz75LFnZCTOsmk_4HaVBGqevu248C04a1jNZoH5jgReuB5BvbcwQ0SaTgPfpkYom6H0Y13FNkrMkQUlZFiXmLRXGXyUCJtbGwm6zZwTI_6-snKODorGJIqwWOTVN2Lg2qSe97ZLy0SA2JjeIpKjLL-BNSuRrf8Towmvv1Pvs0ouCkK87s04/L5AXY7CKHE-My6W8cE_cgWVCkmYiQQu7/22)

**Please use the secure link above to receive your video series on Russia immediately.**

Warm regards,

Larry P. Arnn

Buffalo County Republicans represented in the Mondovi Friendship Day Parade on Sunday, June 28th! **Chippewa County**
Attendees at the Stanley Rodeo Parade on June 20th saw Republicans of Chippewa County walking alongside their elephant float! **Green County**
Republicans of Green County held high-quality events over the last two weeks. They hosted Brittany Kinser from Kids Win Wisconsin, Jon Aleckson for 50th Assembly District, and State Representative Todd Novak at their monthly Breakfast Meeting on the 20th. Five days later, they teamed up with Dane County Republicans for a fundraising event for State Senator Howard Marklein, who spoke alongside former Congressman Scott Klug. The following Sunday the 28th, members had a great time at New Glarus Picnic in the Park with Jon Aleckson. **Monroe County**
Republicans of Monroe County packed their schedule over the past few weeks. They descended on 215 S. Water Street in Sparta to witness the grand opening of their Campaign HQ for the 2026 cycle. Alongside county party members, Rep. Nancy VanderMeer, Cedric Schnitzler for 95th Assembly, Chris Weaver for Sheriff, Mike Krause for Sheriff, Regional Director for Tiffany Campaign Dave Estenson, and RPW's own Christina Estenson showed up for support. Nate Pollnow, endorsed candidate for Secretary of State, also stopped by the new HQ on his way to the Tomah Tractor Pull, where county party members were tabling. Members remarkably still found time to support local law enforcement over two Back the Blue Mondays. Great work, Monroe County! **Racine County**
Racine GOP members attended a kickoff event for a state assembly campaign, where State Rep. Scott Wittke and former Lt. Gov Rebecca Kleefisch teamed up to announce retired Air Force Lt. Colonel Gina Paulick's 'District 66' campaign! **Rusk County**
To kick off June, Republicans of Rusk County celebrated the grand opening of their county office in Ladysmith, now open Monday-Wednesday-Friday from 1-5 PM. They also participated in the Sheldon Flag Day parade on June 14th! **St. Croix County**
St. Croix County Republicans kept busy the last few weeks. They prayed together for their monthly community prayer meeting on June 24th, hosted Rep. Rob Kreibich on Save Wisconsin Saturday, and gathered for Pizza and Postcards for Tom Tiffany on July 2nd. **Waukesha County**
On June 28th, Waukesha County Republicans marched with their elephant float in back-to-back parades: the Hartland Hometown Celebration parade and the Kettle Moraine Days Parade! _**by Lawrence Winnerman**_
#### It is the second week of October, and the light is going out of the sky over a quarter section outside Holdrege, Nebraska, and the man in the combine cab is fifty-eight years old and bringing in a crop that is mostly not there.
There is an empty seat beside him. For nine years the man who filled it rode this cab through every harvest. In July they took him in a raid, and the seat has been empty since.
The farmer can read the ruin on the yield monitor, a number he has watched sink all afternoon like a fever going the wrong way--a little under half of what this ground gave two years ago. He did not grow bad corn; a careful man does not spend a fortune raising corn he cannot sell. He grew the best corn he could on the acres he had already committed before the worst of the prices hit, and then he watched the nitrogen he had counted on for the rest arrive at a number he could not pay. So the far quarter, the ground that has been corn since his father's time, stands in soybeans this year, because soybeans pull their nitrogen out of the air and ask him for almost nothing. Across the fence the beans are the color of an old bruise. On his side the corn is short and pale, the lower leaves fired yellow up the midrib, the ears light in the husk, and he knew before the elevator could tell him that this grain will grade down and dock him on the way across the scale.
The pivots ran all summer. He can see their tracks worn into ground that should not have needed the water, and he can still feel the fuel in his teeth--the most expensive diesel of his farming life, close to double two winters ago--because the same thing that put the price on his fuel put it on every inch of water he pulled out of the earth to keep a hot, dry summer from taking the whole crop. It took half of it anyway.
He could have survived any one of these. A dry summer he has survived before; a bad fuel year, a thin fertilizer year--any one of them, a farm is built to take one at a time. What a farm is not built to take is all of them in the same year, stacked, each one landing on a margin the last one had already stripped.
There is a propane tank behind the shed that has to dry this wet corn before it can go in the bin and then heat the house when the cold comes, and he has already been quoted the winter price. There is an empty hook in the barn where most Octobers a steer hangs for the freezer; this year the hay ran dearer than the animal, so the steer went to the sale barn early, and the freezer will stay empty. And still, at first light, he greased the pivot and climbed into the cab and went out to bring in what there was, because that is what you do.
Sometimes, there's nothing to be done but the doing, and the doing is the last thing they cannot take.
None of it was his mistake. He read the markets. He worked the ground his father worked. He did everything a careful man is told to do, and he will lose money for the fourth year running--better than a hundred and sixty thousand dollars on his thousand acres. And he will not name the man who did this to him.
It is not that he can't.
He knows the name as well as I do. It is that naming it would mean admitting who he believed, who he defended at his own kitchen table, who he stood in line one November to vote for--and what that trust has cost him. His heart was broken once already, quietly, somewhere between the ballot and the yield monitor. To say the name out loud now would be to break it again, on purpose, with his own mouth. So he doesn't. He just drives.
I will say it for him.
He has earned the right to look away. I have not.
He did not start the war that ended with the strait sealed and his fertilizer stranded behind it. He did not order the tariffs that ran up the price of his fuel, his parts, his seed. He did not sign the proclamation that conceded, in the language of hurricanes and floods, that the American food supply had become an emergency. He did none of it. One man did all of it.
Donald Trump made every one of these choices, and not one was forced on him. The war was a choice. The tariffs were a choice. The proclamation was a choice--a signature on a Monday, dressed as rescue from a fire he lit himself. What emptied this combine was not a storm, and not a market, and not an act of God.
**It was a man at a desk who will never see this field, and his decision has been traveling toward it --across the closed water, through the ruined spring, like a murder hornet hot on a honeybee--every day since he made it.**

# The Document Nobody Read
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba4d313-821c-4c4e-ab85-f19927805828?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### On June 29, 2026, Donald Trump signed a proclamation, and almost no one read it.
There was no address, no split screen, no scroll; it moved the way paperwork moves--a declaration of emergency and a schedule of duties suspended. For eight months, phosphate fertilizer from the Kingdom of Morocco will enter the United States free of the duties that have sat on it for years. The stated reason is a threat to the nation's food supply.
The authority is Section 318 of the Tariff Act of 1930. Read the statute and see what it is for. It lets the President, in an emergency "by reason of a state of war, or otherwise," permit "the importation free of duty of food, clothing, and medical, surgical, and other supplies for use in emergency relief work." It is the law you reach for after the hurricane, after the flood, after the shelling stops--when a place has been stripped bare and the trucks of relief need to move without waiting on the tariff schedule. For most of a century, that is what it has been: the statute of the aftermath.
This time the relief supply is fertilizer. And the disaster it answers has not visibly happened yet.
A government does not reach for its disaster law over a problem it believes is small. It does not classify a thing as catastrophe in the paperwork and expect you to read the classification as routine. The proclamation is written in the language of relief, and relief is an admission that harm is already on the way.
Read plainly, it is not reassurance. It is a confession--filed by the man who started the fire.
His own administration's numbers say how large the harm is. The Department of Agriculture estimates the move will cut phosphate prices by roughly 22 percent and save farmers about $1.82 billion across more than 100,000 farms and 97 million acres.
Those are not the figures of a rounding error. They are the figures of a government reaching for the nearest lever it can still pull--because the man in charge has already pulled all the others the wrong way.

# The Valve They Could Reach
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba4d313-821c-4c4e-ab85-f19927805828?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### To see how little the proclamation can fix, you have to know that "fertilizer" is three different problems wearing one word.
Crops need nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium; each comes from a different place, is made a different way, and answers to a different shock. Trump moved on exactly one of them.
Phosphate was the one he could touch, because the barrier on Moroccan phosphate was never geology or distance--it was a tariff the United States had itself placed on Morocco's state producer. A tariff is a valve with a handle in Washington, and it opens with a signature. That is all June 29 was: the government letting go of a pressure it had built itself, on the one input where the blockage was its own doing.
Nitrogen has no such easy handle. Nitrogen fertilizer--urea, ammonia--is made from natural gas, and the Gulf ships roughly a third of the world's exported urea; Iran and Qatar are the two largest exporters on earth, and most of what they make can leave only through the Strait of Hormuz.
When Trump foolishly joined Israel in an air war on Iran at the end of February, and Iran answered by declaring the strait closed in early March, that third of the world's urea went behind a locked door. Qatar's great urea works--the single largest on the planet--went dark. Urea passed $850 a metric ton, up by roughly 80 percent in two months, its highest since the spring of 2022. The World Bank expects the global fertilizer price index up more than 30 percent across the year.
And even the phosphate is not fully his to free. Phosphate fertilizer is cooked with sulfur--turned to sulfuric acid to break down the rock--and close to half the world's traded sulfur comes from the same Gulf now behind the same locked door; sulfur, too, ran to record highs. Trump can lift the tariff at the border and still not touch the sulfur that sets the price at the plant. He freed the one input he could reach, and reached only partway into it--after shutting the ones he could not.
_**You cannot sign away a blockade you started. The proclamation does not solve the fertilizer crisis. It marks, precisely, the part of the crisis its author has no way to take back.**_

# Three Clocks
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba4d313-821c-4c4e-ab85-f19927805828?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### Here is what makes this a hinge and not a headline: fertilizer is not a grocery item, it is an input, and an input does not travel from the dock to the shelf.
It travels through a crop, and a crop takes a season. Between the shock and the price you pay there is a lag--and the lag is why the danger is nearly invisible now. There is not one clock in this story. There are three, and they keep different time.
The first clock you can hear. Nitrogen does not keep; it is restless in the soil, it leaches with the rain and gasses off into the air, so a corn crop needs it laid down fresh every spring or the crop is simply not there. That is the clock that already struck the field outside Holdrege. The nitrogen a farmer could not get last spring is a yield he does not have this fall, a bushel that never crosses the scale because it never grew.
The second clock runs now, between the field and the shelf. Roughly 70 percent of farmers told the Farm Bureau this spring that they could not afford all the fertilizer they needed; corn acreage fell about 3 percent, and much of the corn that did go in went in hungry. None of that reaches a store in 2026. It reaches the harvest, then the grain stocks, then the feed, then the meat and the bread and the whole middle of the grocery store. We have watched this clock before: when fertilizer spiked in 2022, growers were briefly spared because the inputs for that crop had been bought the year before, and the pain came a season late--the only way it ever comes.
It is coming now, for 2027.
The third clock is the one almost no one is watching, because it makes no sound at all. Corn needs phosphorus and potassium too, and those keep nothing like nitrogen's time. They do not wash away in a season; they hold in the soil, a reserve built up over years of patient care. So a farmer facing a doubled phosphate bill and a potash bill he cannot carry has an option nitrogen never gives him: he can skip a year.
He can draw the reserve down, plant into the fertility already in the ground, and lose almost nothing this season--and every extension agronomist in the country is telling him, correctly, to do exactly that. So across tens of millions of acres, quietly, in the same year, farmers begin spending down the fertility bank in their own soil to make the numbers work. There is no failure in 2026, and none in 2027. The ground looks the same. And then, somewhere past 2028, on soil mined one lean year to outlast a war one man chose, the yields begin to sink on fields no one thought to worry about.
_**The bill for the cheapest year comes due as the most expensive one. It comes due with interest. And the collateral is the land itself.**_
Three clocks, then, wound by the same hand and set to strike in three different years. No one intended this particular farmer's ruin--but every lever that produced it was pulled on purpose, by one man, in plain sight. Remember the difference. Because when the bill finally comes due, they will erase it--they will file authored harm and dumb accident under the same word, and hand it to you as if the two were ever the same thing.
They will tell you it was nobody.

# The Hope Priced Into the Number
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/0ba4d313-821c-4c4e-ab85-f19927805828?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
#### You would not know any of this from the price of oil.
Brent crude, which ran past $120 a barrel at the height of the war in the spring, had fallen back below $72 by midsummer, on the expectation that the ceasefire will hold and the strait will reopen. Read the tape and you would think the emergency had passed.
Read the water and you would not. The ships have not come back; the flows through Hormuz are still assumed shut, the resumption always another quarter away. The market is not pricing what is happening--it is pricing what it prays will happen. And the official food forecasts wear the same false calm.
The Department of Agriculture expects grocery prices to rise only about 2.5 percent this year, a number that looks like nothing and means nothing, because it is the reading from before the clock strikes. It reflects a crop planted and largely priced before the worst of the shock, and it will not survive the 2027 harvest. Even now the seams show: the same agency already expects beef up 7.5 percent, and the most aggressive private forecasters warn that the fertilizer shock could push food into the double digits as the lag lands next year.
And fertilizer carries a cruelty oil does not. Even if the strait opened tomorrow and the tankers sailed by Friday, the season is already spent. The nitrogen not laid down last spring cannot be laid down retroactively on a crop already in the ground or already given up.
**You cannot re-plant a spring.**
Whatever reopening the market is hoping for comes too late for the harvest that sets next year's price.

#### So let us be careful with the word nobody.
They are going to tell you nobody did this. When the receipt lands in 2027--when the beef and the bread climb and keep climbing--you will be told it was inflation, weather, forces, the war, the market. You will be told it was nobody. That lie is the most valuable thing he owns.
Because it was not nobody. It was one man, and I have already named him. Donald Trump started the war that sealed the strait. Donald Trump ran the tariffs up the side of every input a farm depends on. Donald Trump signed the proclamation that admitted the emergency he had manufactured. Each was a choice, freely made, and the word nobody is the door he is counting on to walk through before the bill arrives.
And the bill arrives on the people with the least room to carry it. It falls on the man in the cab with the empty seat beside him. It falls on the family already doing the arithmetic in the cereal aisle, and on the woman on the fixed income who will eat a little less this winter and teach herself to call it a preference.
Here is the cruelest part of the trick: the door he walks through is held open by the very people he hurt. The men who made the money already moved it; they will be fine--they always are. But they do not hide behind their own innocence. They hide behind his loyalty. The man in the cab knows the name and will not say it, because saying it would cost him his own heart--and that silence, multiplied across ten thousand kitchen tables, is the alibi. They are counting on every good man who believed to love the liar more than he can bear to name him.
That is the part I refuse.
I refuse to let the word nobody launder a man's signature into an act of God. Tracing the mechanism was never the same as excusing it--it was how we followed the wire back to the hand on the switch. And the hand has a name.
So say it--not at the man beside you at the elevator, but with him, and for him, until the day the cost is so plain that even a broken heart can say it out loud. Say the number, and say the name beside it. Say it to the woman in the aisle next year when the receipt proves you right. Name the decision, the date, and the man who made it. Refuse to be surprised, and refuse to be surprised alone, because the one thing he cannot survive is a harm that arrives already named, out loud, by many, before it lands.
The price is already written. It was written in a field outside Holdrege in October, in the distance between what a careful man needed and what he was allowed to get, in the empty seat where a man he trusted used to ride.
The only thing still unwritten is whether we let the word nobody walk him out of the room.
**So when they hand you the receipt and tell you it is nobody 's fault, look them in the eye and give them back the name. **
**Then say it again.**
**And again.**
**Until it is the first thing anyone thinks of when the price comes due --and until the farmer in the cab can say it too, not to lose his heart, but to take it back.**

A quiet emergency proclamation, filed under the law you reach for after a hurricane, just confessed what's coming for the price of food. | | and | Jul 7 | | | ---|---|--- | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- by Lawrence Winnerman It is the second week of October, and the light is going out of the sky over a quarter section outside Holdrege, Nebraska, and the man in the combine cab is fifty-eight years old and bringing in a crop that is mostly not there. There is an empty seat beside him. For nine years the man who filled it rode this cab through every harvest. In July they took him in a raid, and the seat has been empty since. The farmer can read the ruin on the yield monitor, a number he has watched sink all afternoon like a fever going the wrong way--a little under half of what this ground gave two years ago. He did not grow bad corn; a careful man does not spend a fortune raising corn he cannot sell. He grew the best corn he could on the acres he had already committed before the worst of the prices hit, and then he watched the nitrogen he had counted on for the rest arrive at a number he could not pay. So the far quarter, the ground that has been corn since his father's time, stands in soybeans this year, because soybeans pull their nitrogen out of the air and ask him for almost nothing. Across the fence the beans are the color of an old bruise. On his side the corn is short and pale, the lower leaves fired yellow up the midrib, the ears light in the husk, and he knew before the elevator could tell him that this grain will grade down and dock him on the way across the scale. The pivots ran all summer. He can see their tracks worn into ground that should not have needed the water, and he can still feel the fuel in his teeth--the most expensive diesel of his farming life, close to double two winters ago--because the same thing that put the price on his fuel put it on every inch of water he pulled out of the earth to keep a hot, dry summer from taking the whole crop. It took half of it anyway. He could have survived any one of these. A dry summer he has survived before; a bad fuel year, a thin fertilizer year--any one of them, a farm is built to take one at a time. What a farm is not built to take is all of them in the same year, stacked, each one landing on a margin the last one had already stripped. There is a propane tank behind the shed that has to dry this wet corn before it can go in the bin and then heat the house when the cold comes, and he has already been quoted the winter price. There is an empty hook in the barn where most Octobers a steer hangs for the freezer; this year the hay ran dearer than the animal, so the steer went to the sale barn early, and the freezer will stay empty. And still, at first light, he greased the pivot and climbed into the cab and went out to bring in what there was, because that is what you do. Sometimes, there's nothing to be done but the doing, and the doing is the last thing they cannot take. None of it was his mistake. He read the markets. He worked the ground his father worked. He did everything a careful man is told to do, and he will lose money for the fourth year running--better than a hundred and sixty thousand dollars on his thousand acres. And he will not name the man who did this to him. It is not that he can't. He knows the name as well as I do. It is that naming it would mean admitting who he believed, who he defended at his own kitchen table, who he stood in line one November to vote for--and what that trust has cost him. His heart was broken once already, quietly, somewhere between the ballot and the yield monitor. To say the name out loud now would be to break it again, on purpose, with his own mouth. So he doesn't. He just drives. I will say it for him. He has earned the right to look away. I have not. He did not start the war that ended with the strait sealed and his fertilizer stranded behind it. He did not order the tariffs that ran up the price of his fuel, his parts, his seed. He did not sign the proclamation that conceded, in the language of hurricanes and floods, that the American food supply had become an emergency. He did none of it. One man did all of it. Donald Trump made every one of these choices, and not one was forced on him. The war was a choice. The tariffs were a choice. The proclamation was a choice--a signature on a Monday, dressed as rescue from a fire he lit himself. What emptied this combine was not a storm, and not a market, and not an act of God. It was a man at a desk who will never see this field, and his decision has been traveling toward it --across the closed water, through the ruined spring, like a murder hornet hot on a honeybee--every day since he made it. The Document Nobody Read | | ---|---|--- On June 29, 2026, Donald Trump signed a proclamation, and almost no one read it. There was no address, no split screen, no scroll; it moved the way paperwork moves--a declaration of emergency and a schedule of duties suspended. For eight months, phosphate fertilizer from the Kingdom of Morocco will enter the United States free of the duties that have sat on it for years. The stated reason is a threat to the nation's food supply. The authority is Section 318 of the Tariff Act of 1930. Read the statute and see what it is for. It lets the President, in an emergency "by reason of a state of war, or otherwise," permit "the importation free of duty of food, clothing, and medical, surgical, and other supplies for use in emergency relief work." It is the law you reach for after the hurricane, after the flood, after the shelling stops--when a place has been stripped bare and the trucks of relief need to move without waiting on the tariff schedule. For most of a century, that is what it has been: the statute of the aftermath. This time the relief supply is fertilizer. And the disaster it answers has not visibly happened yet. A government does not reach for its disaster law over a problem it believes is small. It does not classify a thing as catastrophe in the paperwork and expect you to read the classification as routine. The proclamation is written in the language of relief, and relief is an admission that harm is already on the way. Read plainly, it is not reassurance. It is a confession--filed by the man who started the fire. His own administration's numbers say how large the harm is. The Department of Agriculture estimates the move will cut phosphate prices by roughly 22 percent and save farmers about $1.82 billion across more than 100,000 farms and 97 million acres. Those are not the figures of a rounding error. They are the figures of a government reaching for the nearest lever it can still pull--because the man in charge has already pulled all the others the wrong way. The Valve They Could Reach | | ---|---|--- To see how little the proclamation can fix, you have to know that "fertilizer" is three different problems wearing one word. Crops need nitrogen, phosphorus, and potassium; each comes from a different place, is made a different way, and answers to a different shock. Trump moved on exactly one of them. Phosphate was the one he could touch, because the barrier on Moroccan phosphate was never geology or distance--it was a tariff the United States had itself placed on Morocco's state producer. A tariff is a valve with a handle in Washington, and it opens with a signature. That is all June 29 was: the government letting go of a pressure it had built itself, on the one input where the blockage was its own doing. Nitrogen has no such easy handle. Nitrogen fertilizer--urea, ammonia--is made from natural gas, and the Gulf ships roughly a third of the world's exported urea; Iran and Qatar are the two largest exporters on earth, and most of what they make can leave only through the Strait of Hormuz. When Trump foolishly joined Israel in an air war on Iran at the end of February, and Iran answered by declaring the strait closed in early March, that third of the world's urea went behind a locked door. Qatar's great urea works--the single largest on the planet--went dark. Urea passed $850 a metric ton, up by roughly 80 percent in two months, its highest since the spring of 2022. The World Bank expects the global fertilizer price index up more than 30 percent across the year. And even the phosphate is not fully his to free. Phosphate fertilizer is cooked with sulfur--turned to sulfuric acid to break down the rock--and close to half the world's traded sulfur comes from the same Gulf now behind the same locked door; sulfur, too, ran to record highs. Trump can lift the tariff at the border and still not touch the sulfur that sets the price at the plant. He freed the one input he could reach, and reached only partway into it--after shutting the ones he could not. You cannot sign away a blockade you started. The proclamation does not solve the fertilizer crisis. It marks, precisely, the part of the crisis its author has no way to take back. Three Clocks | | ---|---|--- Here is what makes this a hinge and not a headline: fertilizer is not a grocery item, it is an input, and an input does not travel from the dock to the shelf. It travels through a crop, and a crop takes a season. Between the shock and the price you pay there is a lag--and the lag is why the danger is nearly invisible now. There is not one clock in this story. There are three, and they keep different time. The first clock you can hear. Nitrogen does not keep; it is restless in the soil, it leaches with the rain and gasses off into the air, so a corn crop needs it laid down fresh every spring or the crop is simply not there. That is the clock that already struck the field outside Holdrege. The nitrogen a farmer could not get last spring is a yield he does not have this fall, a bushel that never crosses the scale because it never grew. The second clock runs now, between the field and the shelf. Roughly 70 percent of farmers told the Farm Bureau this spring that they could not afford all the fertilizer they needed; corn acreage fell about 3 percent, and much of the corn that did go in went in hungry. None of that reaches a store in 2026. It reaches the harvest, then the grain stocks, then the feed, then the meat and the bread and the whole middle of the grocery store. We have watched this clock before: when fertilizer spiked in 2022, growers were briefly spared because the inputs for that crop had been bought the year before, and the pain came a season late--the only way it ever comes. It is coming now, for 2027. The third clock is the one almost no one is watching, because it makes no sound at all. Corn needs phosphorus and potassium too, and those keep nothing like nitrogen's time. They do not wash away in a season; they hold in the soil, a reserve built up over years of patient care. So a farmer facing a doubled phosphate bill and a potash bill he cannot carry has an option nitrogen never gives him: he can skip a year. He can draw the reserve down, plant into the fertility already in the ground, and lose almost nothing this season--and every extension agronomist in the country is telling him, correctly, to do exactly that. So across tens of millions of acres, quietly, in the same year, farmers begin spending down the fertility bank in their own soil to make the numbers work. There is no failure in 2026, and none in 2027. The ground looks the same. And then, somewhere past 2028, on soil mined one lean year to outlast a war one man chose, the yields begin to sink on fields no one thought to worry about. The bill for the cheapest year comes due as the most expensive one. It comes due with interest. And the collateral is the land itself. Three clocks, then, wound by the same hand and set to strike in three different years. No one intended this particular farmer's ruin--but every lever that produced it was pulled on purpose, by one man, in plain sight. Remember the difference. Because when the bill finally comes due, they will erase it--they will file authored harm and dumb accident under the same word, and hand it to you as if the two were ever the same thing. They will tell you it was nobody. The Hope Priced Into the Number | | ---|---|--- You would not know any of this from the price of oil. Brent crude, which ran past $120 a barrel at the height of the war in the spring, had fallen back below $72 by midsummer, on the expectation that the ceasefire will hold and the strait will reopen. Read the tape and you would think the emergency had passed. Read the water and you would not. The ships have not come back; the flows through Hormuz are still assumed shut, the resumption always another quarter away. The market is not pricing what is happening--it is pricing what it prays will happen. And the official food forecasts wear the same false calm. The Department of Agriculture expects grocery prices to rise only about 2.5 percent this year, a number that looks like nothing and means nothing, because it is the reading from before the clock strikes. It reflects a crop planted and largely priced before the worst of the shock, and it will not survive the 2027 harvest. Even now the seams show: the same agency already expects beef up 7.5 percent, and the most aggressive private forecasters warn that the fertilizer shock could push food into the double digits as the lag lands next year. And fertilizer carries a cruelty oil does not. Even if the strait opened tomorrow and the tankers sailed by Friday, the season is already spent. The nitrogen not laid down last spring cannot be laid down retroactively on a crop already in the ground or already given up. You cannot re-plant a spring. Whatever reopening the market is hoping for comes too late for the harvest that sets next year's price. So let us be careful with the word nobody. They are going to tell you nobody did this. When the receipt lands in 2027--when the beef and the bread climb and keep climbing--you will be told it was inflation, weather, forces, the war, the market. You will be told it was nobody. That lie is the most valuable thing he owns. Because it was not nobody. It was one man, and I have already named him. Donald Trump started the war that sealed the strait. Donald Trump ran the tariffs up the side of every input a farm depends on. Donald Trump signed the proclamation that admitted the emergency he had manufactured. Each was a choice, freely made, and the word nobody is the door he is counting on to walk through before the bill arrives. And the bill arrives on the people with the least room to carry it. It falls on the man in the cab with the empty seat beside him. It falls on the family already doing the arithmetic in the cereal aisle, and on the woman on the fixed income who will eat a little less this winter and teach herself to call it a preference. Here is the cruelest part of the trick: the door he walks through is held open by the very people he hurt. The men who made the money already moved it; they will be fine--they always are. But they do not hide behind their own innocence. They hide behind his loyalty. The man in the cab knows the name and will not say it, because saying it would cost him his own heart--and that silence, multiplied across ten thousand kitchen tables, is the alibi. They are counting on every good man who believed to love the liar more than he can bear to name him. That is the part I refuse. I refuse to let the word nobody launder a man's signature into an act of God. Tracing the mechanism was never the same as excusing it--it was how we followed the wire back to the hand on the switch. And the hand has a name. So say it--not at the man beside you at the elevator, but with him, and for him, until the day the cost is so plain that even a broken heart can say it out loud. Say the number, and say the name beside it. Say it to the woman in the aisle next year when the receipt proves you right. Name the decision, the date, and the man who made it. Refuse to be surprised, and refuse to be surprised alone, because the one thing he cannot survive is a harm that arrives already named, out loud, by many, before it lands. The price is already written. It was written in a field outside Holdrege in October, in the distance between what a careful man needed and what he was allowed to get, in the empty seat where a man he trusted used to ride. The only thing still unwritten is whether we let the word nobody walk him out of the room. So when they hand you the receipt and tell you it is nobody 's fault, look them in the eye and give them back the name. Then say it again. And again. Until it is the first thing anyone thinks of when the price comes due --and until the farmer in the cab can say it too, not to lose his heart, but to take it back. Cliff 's Note: One last thing, and then we'll let you go. Work like this--weeks of reporting, sourced and triple-checked, unwilling to let the word nobody do the powerful's job for them--only stays free if enough of you help carry it. ## Assault Accusation Derails Platner Senate Race
Graham Platner, the Democrats' Senate nominee in Maine, [paused campaign events](https://email.editor.jointheflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAURL8Gd1iAibELim3cZdstrRu42KyucQQkbP5-5af3B6870kgzOvPnvt4hUkzbbzjQ1nCuCVshrBXz6vEor7zhk6AmzC3W3WdoQKsSauTCcGFWD5E-q-68DYgKhw6tNNOg5SxuY7fbyY9ohAtOz9NtnqV8jM4NcpiC1ujF0EV7tQkjjBRS6LlXQbpBm-BmHIOEkWmBPtYz93_PmOqOgT7nG3PvzqMju9f6LGz4xdTC1NJa692jXBZXztRyIVPLlmGHg3-78ANiQl4wQUWewV387wXEoRR4UeVAhBvUeCamli5b_2yRKJbRMC22AyJ97dcfnfa26n8AAAD__5ilg0A) Monday after being accused of sexual assault, as Sen. Minority Leader Chuck Schumer and Sen. Kirsten Gillibrand, along with the Maine Democratic Party, urged him to withdraw from the race. ## Texas Stock Exchange Begins Trading
The Texas Stock Exchange [began trading on Monday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0L2SrCAQBeCnwUyraRGuAcFNzGbTDSkGmpFaRixhR-ftt7Rqn2Dz_jnf-byZm40pLo8P-yRdj5DNQntJVCttptJhS6nZfdHhZrs8KK-0lNUaBJQtqBaU8TamtxGN13fwI29Ic_WvF4hcYTNrNYjgA_fBB-FwGMfeKSmExSDkHaBvoj6PgQLFOeCA3YhegKTBC4dcWc4EkI81b12d6YoU0ju_aOtcfjZJz7WuhfX_GU4Mp33fu5APlHP-LjUv5xDD6VQxnK719iK1v6b2QjWb9useU4pFKibg8bQxXR_q33p5afwJAAD__28MeKY) in Dallas, opening the most well-funded challenge to the New York Stock Exchange and NASDAQ in decades. The phased rollout starts with member broker-dealers, banks, and trading firms trading test stocks, with thousands of equities coming online through July. Exchange-traded funds are expected this fall, corporate listings by year's end, and the [first IPOs in early 2027](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkbGSqzoMhp8GOmVsBTAUFLeh29uekhG2nHjW2CxWQvL2Z8jMPsGpVGj06_ukP1_zF4UY0u1_WnmUl89z4qNEFuF9Fn5RKZLtN7_sndKN88apbDSjwg6UAWVmRyG-56Z246LcoGsetemvDaI2WN_HflDGdb1f7NJRP2iDxGQ8L4u2hjzXYTzDlFFGa4UtXgZ0jeq4dY1FbUhXjWIXJO8XufMHycd3fvJ-sXmt43gX2Up1_a_CqcLpOI7LN6fSnt0KJ9ol2MgVTqdYhVPMlmKF0yfpt8LHEn41wVGMVOCgGKHIziyQqDj6gfQuDD4kSpYhpCcXCekG_PMIErhA2DKw-AJsc8rrG5ZHCYnLuYJ2eWwgO7lzxOZ1oxT4hEBzBe3bVuvGAdtBQ-N6DwN3CN4tpNrFGNVd63102xFiDKUzVaNuK4X4uYP82_eeI_4NAAD__6cTsvQ). The Dallas-based startup is backed by $275 million from investors including [BlackRock and Citadel Securities](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJyk0LGyozAMBdCvgU4Z2TgxFC62Sfe23ZJRsADvMzZjawLv73fIL2wv3Tn3_vkavyjEkJbftLGTc85j4qNGFuEyCp9Uq-Tpm89ppbRw3jnVnUaN-gFoAe3oKcSf0bTevdAPqmWnbN8ZrZXV7erMgD0O_aCsGe7oiazivnv11NupI4NtcFcYWrRKob7r26C9wQffvZm0sqQag-yD5HKTlT-kOf7kN5fblLc2ulVkr033q9HPRj89xUg1pJTfJFyvm0Y_5axc4S-_YOVUqVyVIScg6BA3OKjAtHIVoPINMVQJaalAyQOBFEp15gJ7LkIR5piP610yfDSNfrbF-f0IMYb6sI3BZaMQPzz5v1HfTv8LAAD__wo3jhs). Since TXSE announced its plans in 2024, the NYSE and NASDAQ have each opened Texas branches.
## Justices Won't Block Texas App Law
The U.S. [Supreme Court declined Monday](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGyqyAQhp8GO5xlY0QLitvY5bandBCWyASFARKTtz9jXuE0O1vs7Pf9_89tvmkf_H7_rzdS9e3ivNNRAtVKea701qXUaB70Nqve7xQT7SXpGQF7DpKDnK324TN3jVUL2FE0pIQcLh2ikNisqpfOyWEZDZgLDj3iYHrnXGfAWRLL2Hh1PgMJUgjAK7Yj2g56utrOoJBasA7I-hpzW1f6KrnwiS_KrYlbE9Raayrs8o_hxHA6jqNNMfjqTTwPGE5nIobTiWE4gTzHuZVnyrQRN_GZK7dkgt-p8Br5EqJ58C-L65R4qTETD_rgAOMgBzE2Wdl0-BB86SXr4L5pH75C9W81vhT-BgAA__-OfIZg) to block Texas' App Store Accountability Act, leaving the age-verification law in force while a First Amendment challenge plays out. The law requires app stores to verify every user's age and to link minors' accounts to a parent, who [must approve each download](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGu4yAQRb8Gd0Qwj5ikoNjG3dt2S2sCYwctARbGcfL3K-cXXnt1de7R_fM9f2NMMa-_8UGOX0uZM-09ETO1memFvXPxf-nl75hXKpVyrziDglEqK5WdA8b0ns0Q3E2Fqx7IaXv5MgDawnB343LRZ7zQFczNjuNilaIl2FsI4JU_myG6A6asslorOMPpCsGokc7BeNAWtTCKQuTSTnynj9KS3uVJ7eTLY0juzly7-PolYBIw7ft-6r7w1m-prEdFwHQsCJiUFTD1rTZ6kPRlaywxpbJ3-cFKLpLyUponmXCXjf5tscW8SlxJPqnFJXrkWLLEHGTFRpkxSV9yp8zyyGsVMA3NhbrHlGIfrTBqfWBMH1v-2cdPB_8DAAD__xBak9o) or purchase. A federal judge in Austin blocked it in December, but the 5th Circuit revived it last month. Attorney General Ken Paxton, backed by 27 other state attorneys general, defended the law. "_Texas has not only the right, but the duty, to protect children from the harms of our modern digital space_ ," [he said after the appeals court ruling](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkLGO2zAQRL9G6iiQNG2eCxZp3F3alMKaHEvM0aRCri3r7wMZyRdct8A-DN7Mr8_xk2KKefpJdzh-3cqYsbYEZtSR8aLWuPgvvPxMeUJZkNtCo5b6JKQV0o6BYtpG0wd3leGsejhlPw5Ga2V1PzuQNuebNzhAWXk-XHEM4SN4D6NIXU0f3R4mrbRKSX3Uw1kHI084BuO1sqQ6IxEilzrwjLfSLW3liTr4cu-Tm5mX1h1-dPrS6cu6rsMbIuZSM7YJGZXSMJVnpy97u05fKhKoYT__c-IfKL6QxUIvLlk0-EdFE3f6Xap4Rs-lbmKpheE55kn4OaZQkUXJKWaIij-PWPcPTeirC8saU4rtZDsjpzvF9Jbm7039dPpvAAAA__8CGJoh). The challengers, a trade group representing Apple and Google and a coalition of Texas students, argue the law restricts lawful speech for adults and minors alike. Trade group president Matt Schruers [said such choices](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkL2ypCAQhZ8GMyxomcEJCDYxu5tuaPWFHqUuAgXM6Lz9lu4jbPr1T33n_Pmav9AHH5ffuJFpxzPNkfYaqDUqc6MDa23J_tBhV4wLpUyxZpxBwJ0LzYWeHfrwmVXnzLdwD9mRkXocFIDU0K2GrCT61m54KDXe0MqRSA4jDNY95aBc5835TGihpRRwg_4BTok73ZyyIDVKpgQ531Lp20qX0jN80ptKb9PWBbO2lisbfjGYGEz7vvc_B8ZzyGA60zCYrjOeU_DN2wusvvJ_FHPmtaVCPODObXoFxwvVFTPxFIOPxNFaqpVj5fWVC210rpXGbYrVOyqV2xVDoLgQg6krxuXdh-DrXTMllg19uGTb_1X8NvA3AAD__5kElOU) "should be made around the dinner table, not the governor's desk."
## Off-Duty Firefighter Saves Three Children
An off-duty Midlothian firefighter pulled [three children from beneath a capsized boat](https://email.editor.thetexasflyover.com/c/eJykkDGO5CAQRU-DM1pFGRsTONjE2Wy6oVWGoo2GMRYw7e49_arnCht_6em_9-dj_aCY4nH_TV88t2fI68FXTdwal7Xxk2pt2X3y0-103DmffNSTVgQcJRgJZvUU02vVnZ838FZ1PCsz9RpRGez2GWHqgxt7Ig0W_GjBKOZgw6Yd90Z1cX7DwIBRCnDAm0WvYeTBa4fKkBIa2MeWy63t_HMppFd-cLm5_NWleW_trKL_JXARuFzXdbsC0XsUuFBp0SUWuLy9BC4pO0oClxyC9N_tJUMsHOJ9b1xk4eq-ucpeuj0mX_iQrdB5speOzhr_spdbpiYpPaiQzzLR5xuOk5FmU6OfbC9pGyapcRrkBsBShc3abXAOgu3K7M8rphTraISG-xfF9OPR_q_-Y8Z_AQAA__-SxJjq) on Alvarado Lake on July 4, reviving two who had stopped breathing. Jason Horne, a medic and firefighter for 20 years, was on the Johnson County lake with his 12-year-old daughter when a group frantically flagged him down. body:
I am flattered.
# [](https://act.alexvindman.com/go/1135?t=1&akid=854%2E3892029%2ENNCmvO)

Peter —
When you dare to take on Donald Trump’s corruption, you suddenly become a lot of people’s #1 enemy.
This guy called me “human scum” for reporting his illegal phone call.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260707-1&refcode2=854_3892029_NNCmvO&akid=854%2E3892029%2ENNCmvO)
His conspiracy theorist son called me the “Deep State architect” and said it made him “nauseous” thinking of me in the U.S. Senate.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260707-1&refcode2=854_3892029_NNCmvO&akid=854%2E3892029%2ENNCmvO)
Even this guy said I should be arrested and prosecuted for “treason” ... with the presumed penalty being death.
[](https://secure.actblue.com/donate/av-em-q32026?refcode=em260707-1&refcode2=854_3892029_NNCmvO&akid=854%2E3892029%2ENNCmvO)

Musk is the wealthiest person in the world, and Trump’s Super PAC has already raised a record-breaking $300 million. That’s a whole lot of money that they will spend to smear me — especially as polls continue to show that we can win. Every ticket includes a copy of the book. VIP guests will have additional opportunities to meet Dr. Wakefield during an exclusive pre-event reception with **photos, book signings, and light refreshments, as well as an intimate dinner** and extended Q&A following the keynote. _The Bequest_ tells the story of a family's journey to America, where tragedy on the Oregon Trail leaves a **mother fighting to protect her son with autism**. It's a moving tale of courage, sacrifice, resilience, and hope set against the backdrop of the American West. Whether you've followed Dr. Wakefield's work for years or simply enjoy compelling historical fiction, this is a unique opportunity to **hear from him in person and take home a signed copy of his newest book**.
